title: GPU Fleet & Capacity: IaC, CI/CD, and Networking Runbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
# GPU Fleet & Capacity: IaC, CI/CD, and Networking Runbook

Summary
-------
This runbook consolidates our operating procedures, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines, and network requirements for managing Redwood's GPU fleet, capacity planning, and private deployment networking. It is intended for infrastructure engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for capacity, deployments, and incident response.

Scope
-----
- GPU fleet provisioning and autoscaling in cloud accounts (hosted and dedicated).
- Terraform modules and recommended configurations for GPU nodes, autoscalers, and VPC/networking.
- CI/CD pipelines for IaC changes (plan/apply, approvals, drift detection).
- Runbooks for common incidents (capacity shortage, node OOMs, networking faults).
- Onboarding checklist for new regions or private deployments.

Owners and Contacts
-------------------
- Primary owner: infra-gpu-team (owner: Priya Shah)
- Oncall rotation: infra-oncall (see roster in PagerDuty)
- Escalation: Miguel Alvarez (platform lead) -> Anika Bose (eng-sre) -> CTO on-call

High-level Architecture
-----------------------
- GPU node pools: dedicated autoscaled ASGs (or GKE nodepools) per environment and region.
- Control plane components: cluster-autoscaler (or custom autoscaler), provisioning pipelines, and quotas service.
- Persistent storage: NFS/EFS for models where required; prefer ephemeral disk for inference cache when possible.
- Networking: VPC per account with isolated subnets for GPU compute, NAT gateways for egress, and private endpoints for control plane services.

Capacity Planning Principles
---------------------------
- Target steady-state GPU utilization: 60-75% for general-purpose traffic.
- Burst headroom: reserve 15-25% of pool capacity for sudden traffic spikes.
- SLO-driven capacity: plan for 99th percentile latency SLOs - if tail latency increases > 20% under load tests, add capacity.
- Reserve capacity for canary and rollout windows: 5% of pool.

Key Metrics to Track
--------------------
- avg_gpu_utilization (target 0.6-0.75)
- gpu_p95_token_latency (ms)
- node_launch_time P90 (s) < 300s
- pending_pod_seconds (alert if > 120s sustained)
- eviction_rate (alert if > 0.5% / hour)

Sizing & Instance Types
-----------------------
- Current recommended instance families (cloud-neutral guidance):
  - Large/Production: NVIDIA H100-equivalent (8-16 GPU nodes per rack). Example: hpc-h100-8.
  - Balanced: A100-80GB for mixed workloads.
  - Cost-sensitive: A10G / T4 for lower-cost batch/embedding workloads.
- Example node sizing table (reference):
  - model-type: large-gen; vram: 80GB+; node-type: h100-8; recommended-pool-size: 4-128
  - model-type: mid-gen; vram: 40-80GB; node-type: a100-80gb; recommended-pool-size: 4-256
  - model-type: embed-only; vram: 24-40GB; node-type: a10g/t4; recommended-pool-size: 2-128

Autoscaling Policies & Thresholds
--------------------------------
- Horizontal autoscaling (preferred): scale based on queue depth, pending pods, and GPU utilization.
- Example policy (Terraform variable reference):
  - min_replicas: 2
  - target_gpu_utilization_pct: 65
  - scale_up_cooldown_s: 120
  - scale_down_cooldown_s: 600
- Warm pools: maintain a small warm pool (2-4 nodes) per region to reduce cold-start latency for model loads.

Terraform / IaC Modules
----------------------
We maintain reusable modules under infra-terraform-modules. Key modules:
- module/vpc (module name: redwood_vpc) - creates VPC, public/private subnets, NATs, routing tables, and security groups.
- module/gpu_node_pool (module name: redwood_gpu_node_pool) - creates node pools/ASGs with GPU AMI images, instance profile, launch template.
- module/gpu_autoscaler (module name: redwood_gpu_autoscaler) - configures cluster-autoscaler or cloud autoscaling policies, integrates with metrics backend.
- module/iam_roles_and_policies (module name: redwood_iam_roles) - least-privilege roles for node bootstrap, storage access, and KMS.
- module/network_endpoints (module name: redwood_endpoints) - private endpoints for control plane services (S3 endpoints, private API endpoints).

Recommended Module Variables (table)
------------------------------------
- module: redwood_gpu_node_pool
  - region: string
  - instance_type: string
  - gpu_count_per_instance: number
  - min_size: number
  - max_size: number
  - warm_pool_size: number
  - ssh_cidr_blocks: list(string)

Sample Terraform snippet (usage)
-------------------------------
```hcl
module "gpu_pool_west" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/infra-terraform-modules//gpu_node_pool"
  region = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "h100-8"
  gpu_count_per_instance = 8
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 64
  warm_pool_size = 3
}
```

CI/CD: Pipelines and Safe Deployments
------------------------------------
Repository: infra/terraform-gpu
- Branching model: trunk-based. All IaC changes must target main with a PR and at least one approver from infra or security.
- Pipeline stages (example GitHub Actions / CircleCI):
  1. terraform fmt && terraform validate
  2. terraform plan (with workspace per account/environment) - store plan artifact
  3. automatic policy checks (Sentinel/OPAL) and cost-estimate check
  4. PR review & approval (manual gate)
  5. terraform apply in a protected pipeline role (requires at least one approver)
- Drift detection: scheduled daily run that compares state and opens issues for unmanaged changes.
- Canary applies: for large-scale changes (>50% node pool change) apply to canary region/pool first, observe 6 hours, then roll to primary regions.

Approval & Safety Controls
-------------------------
- terraform apply role is limited (apply-bot) and runs from a hardened CI runner.
- Large change threshold: any change that increases a nodepool by > 20% or changes instance_type requires a two-person approval.
- Automated rollback: pipeline captures previous Terraform state snapshot; rollback instructions are generated on failed canary checks.

Networking & Cloud Account Patterns
----------------------------------
- Account model: one cloud account per environment (prod/dedicated/private) and per large customer private deployment where required.
- VPC layout: separate subnets for control, GPU compute, and management services. Use NACLs and security groups to restrict traffic.
- Private endpoints: require S3/Blob private endpoints and private DNS for control plane.
- IP address plan: allocate /20 per region for GPU compute to avoid fragmentation. Document allocations in the central spreadsheet.

Onboarding Checklist for New Region or Private Deployment
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Create cloud account and apply baseline org policies (billing, logging, guardrails).
2. Provision VPC with module/redwood_vpc; verify subnet CIDRs and peering.
3. Create IAM roles using module/redwood_iam_roles; attach to CI runner.
4. Deploy small GPU pool (min_size=2) with module/redwood_gpu_node_pool.
5. Configure autoscaler and metrics export (Prometheus / CloudWatch) via module/redwood_gpu_autoscaler.
6. Run e2e smoke tests: model load, inference latency, cold-start.
7. Add region to monitoring dashboards and alerting playbooks.

Operational Runbooks (Top Incidents)
-----------------------------------
Incident: Capacity Shortage / Pending Pods
1. Verify alerts: pending_pod_seconds and pending_pod_count.
2. Check autoscaler logs and recent events: kubectl describe hpa / cluster-autoscaler logs.
3. If autoscaler failing to scale: check IAM permissions for autoscaler role and API quota errors.
4. Temporary mitigation: scale up nodepool manually with Terraform variable override or cloud console (increase desired capacity by 20%).
5. After remediation: run root-cause analysis and update cluster-autoscaler configuration.

Incident: GPU Node OOM or Driver Crash
1. Collect node logs: journalctl -u nvidia-driver-install.service, dmesg, kubelet logs.
2. Mark node unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node> and drain if necessary.
3. Replace node: terminate instance to trigger reprovision or create replacement via Terraform scale.
4. If OOM is due to model memory: update scheduling requests/limits and add node selectors for higher-VRAM nodes.

Incident: Network Partition / Private Endpoint Failure
1. Verify VPC route tables, NAT gateway status, and security group changes.
2. Check private endpoint health (cloud console) and DNS resolution in VPC.
3. If DNS misconfiguration: verify Route53 (or equivalent) private hosted zone associations.
4. Fallback: route control-plane egress through isolated management NAT or VPN to a healthy region.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures
----------------------------
- Kernel / Driver upgrade: perform in canary pool (1 node), validate driver stability under load for 24h before rolling.
- AMI / Instance-type upgrade: create parallel nodepool with new AMI/type, cordon, drain, and migrate workloads before deleting old pool.
- Terraform rollback: revert the PR and run terraform apply against environment using the saved state snapshot. Document reason in the change log.

Testing and Performance Validation
---------------------------------
- Always run benchmark suite (bench/gpu-load-tests) after significant infra or model changes. Key validations: p50/p95 token latency, cold-start time, and steady-state throughput.
- Load test profile examples:
  - profile: small-chat; concurrency: 200; sequence_length: 512
  - profile: long-context; concurrency: 50; sequence_length: 4096

Cost Controls and Tagging
-------------------------
- Enforce tag policy: environment, team, project, cost-center on all GPU resources.
- Automated nightly job to check for unattached GPUs or idle nodes > 4h and notify owners.
- Prefers spot/preemptible for non-critical batch workloads; reserve on-demand for low-latency production pools.

Documentation & Knowledge Base Links
-----------------------------------
- infra-terraform-modules repo (README + module docs).
- dashboards: /dashboards/gpu-capacity-overview, /dashboards/node-launch-times.
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/template

Appendix: Quick Commands
------------------------
- View pending pods: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep Pending
- Check node GPU utilization (promQL): avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization_pct[5m])
- Trigger manual scale (Terraform): terraform apply -var='gpu_pool_west.min_size=10'
